### workspace rename --help
--- exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: workspace rename [WORKSPACE] NEW [--name WS] [--dry-run] [--json]

Give a stopped worktree workspace a new branch, and with it a new directory,
workspace name and tmux session. Run 'workspace stop' first: a workspace with a
session or a daemon is refused. Nothing is launched afterwards. 'workspace restore'
with the new workspace name resumes its agent conversations; 'workspace launch'
starts new ones. The remote branch is left alone.

The workspace is the one given, else the one the current directory is in. Name it
either as WORKSPACE before NEW or with --name, not both. A rename that stopped
part way prints the command that finishes it: run it again, from anywhere.

Options:
        --name NAME                  The workspace to rename (default: the one detected from the current directory)
        --dry-run                    Print what would change and what is refused; change nothing
        --json                       Print one document (see docs/README.json.md) instead of text, which goes
                                     to stderr; a refusal is the error envelope
    -h, --help                       Show this help

Examples:
  workspace rename fix-login-v2    # rename the stopped workspace you are in to the branch fix-login-v2
  workspace rename --dry-run fix-login-v2    # show the plan and any refusal; change nothing
  workspace rename myproject.worktree-fix-login fix-login-v2    # name the workspace first, from anywhere
  workspace rename fix-login-v2 --name myproject.worktree-fix-login    # the same, naming it with a flag
  workspace rename fix-login-v2 --json    # one document with the plan, warnings and the next step
--- stderr
--- end

### workspace rename --bogus
--- exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
invalid option: --bogus
--- end

### workspace rename
